title: World Action Models: A Survey
hook: Robots are learning to imagine the future before acting. This survey untangles 'world action models' from video generators and VLA policies — and finds them converging on one idea.
key_points: World Action Models (WAMs) are embodied models that predict the future specifically to inform action.
The survey draws lines between world models, video generators, action-grounded video world models, VLA policies, and WAMs.
It organizes methods by what they must generate: rendered futures, latent futures, or video-generation-free action reasoning.
It also decomposes each by predictive substrate, backbone, action coupling, and deployment regime.
Emerging pattern: generate less of the future while keeping exactly what control needs — trading richness against compute, latency, and label cost.
content_html: "World Action Models" (WAMs) are embodied predictive-action models: they forecast the future and make that forecast available to action. The space has exploded — some WAMs repurpose large video generation models, others lean on language or vision-language backbones — and the boundaries with world models, video generators, and Vision-Language-Action policies have blurred. Shen, Liao, Yan, Wang and colleagues offer a common account.
extra_html:
What it organizes

The survey first clarifies the boundaries, then uses two complementary views. One asks what each method must generate — rendered futures, latent futures, or video-generation-free action reasoning. The other decomposes each method by predictive substrate, backbone, action coupling, and deployment regime. Together these support a unified discussion of interactability, causality, persistence, physical plausibility, and generalization.

The pattern it finds

Across these axes a consistent design principle emerges: WAMs are not simply video generators with an action head bolted on. They are predictive-action methods whose choices trade representational richness against compute, memory, latency, and the cost of action labels. The field is moving toward generating less of the future while preserving exactly what control requires — a useful lens for anyone tracking embodied AI.

related.title: World Models Lack a Persistent State
related.hook: Today's video world models render great frames but treat the world like a tracking shot: look away and back, and off-screen events freeze instead of running on — the moon keeps orbiting unwatched.

related.title: World Models Meet Language Models
related.hook: A world model can imagine what happens next; an LLM can reason about it. The hard part is knowing when to trust the daydream — and when the simulation is just plausible nonsense.

related.title: Geometric Action Model: One Backbone for Geometry and Action
related.hook: GAM turns a pretrained 3D-geometry model into a robot's brain - a single backbone that forecasts both future geometry and the actions to get there, beating heavier VLA baselines.

flashcards.back_html: A WAM predicts the future specifically to make it available to action — its design is driven by what control requires, not just by producing realistic video.
